summary: The 'Story' page of a four-page microsite (Story, Design, Origins, Products; only Story was captured). It tells how a Soviet-Estonian children's-book typeface became GT Eesti, as a picture book on black: short chapters with looping flat illustrations of children's-book characters, and each chapter set one weight heavier than the last, so reading the story walks through the family from Ultra Light to Ultra Bold.

instances.look: Two round smiling blond children's faces (flat yellow hair, red cheeks) side by side on black, 'GT Eesti' in large white letters beneath, and a red four-line subtitle 'This is the story of the typeface GT Eesti, from its origins in Soviet Russia in 1940 to its rebirth in Switzerland 2016.'
instances.ux: A ruled tab bar sits above the faces (Story in red as the current page, Design, Origins, Products, Free Trials ↗, Purchase ↗). The faces are looping videos
instances.learn: Use characters drawn in the style of the source material (Estonian children's books) as the mascots of the whole site

instances.ux: Scroll to read; the illustrations loop. The text gets heavier chapter by chapter
instances.learn: Step the type weight up with each chapter (headings Display Ultra Light → Ultra Bold, paragraphs Text Ultra Light → Bold): the narrative itself becomes the weight waterfall

reconstruction.content: Real history: Zhurnalnaya Roublennaya (Anatoly Schukin, 1947), Soviet Estonia 1944–1991, Urs Lehni's students Reto Moser and Tobias Rechsteiner digitising it from children's books in 2009, Display and Text versions, Cyrillics, a 2015 visit to Prof. Ivar Sakk in Tallinn
